methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Late Stage → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.2x) to $52M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 8 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Kinova Robotics is a late-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Charles Deguire and Louis-Joseph L'Ecuyer that has raised $51.6M to date. The robotics and manufacturing sector includes one public comparable and eight private peers, though peers at equivalent stage and valuation tier are limited.

A peer-median approach proved inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the narrow valuation tier; the broader peer set of eight robotics companies does not yield three or more datapoints meeting tight stage and scale filters. Consequently, stage-progression methodology was the primary analytical approach. Using total capital raised ($52M) as a base value proxy and applying a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical for Late Stage progression yields an implied valuation of $62M. This reflects the typical equity expansion expected between late-stage capital rounds and potential exit or growth-stage recapitalization.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $53M to $71M, centered on $62M. The range spans ±15% around the median to account for variance in stage-progression assumptions and unobserved market comparables. Key uncertainties include the absence of direct peer valuation data at equivalent stage and the reliance on a single methodological pillar; additional precision would require either expanded comparable data within robotics manufacturing or revenue and growth metrics to support revenue multiple approaches.
